home.heroTitle: Bridging the Digital Divide for Southeast Asian Indigenous Languages
home.heroSubtitle: With over 800 languages in Malaysia and Indonesia, most critically endangered, IndigiSEA will establish the people, processes, and partnerships essential for long-term linguistic sustainability. The project will develop ethical frameworks, participatory research models, and digital platforms that foster access, innovation, and community leadership to advance ethical digital futures for Indigenous languages.

about.headerSubtitle: Understanding the challenges and our approach to preserving Southeast Asian indigenous languages
problemParagraphs: Southeast Asia is home to an extraordinary linguistic diversity, with over 800 languages spoken across Malaysia and Indonesia alone. However, this rich heritage faces an unprecedented threat.

Most of these languages are critically endangered, with dwindling numbers of speakers and limited documentation. As older generations pass, invaluable linguistic knowledge, cultural traditions, and unique worldviews risk being lost forever.

The digital divide further exacerbates this crisis. While technology has advanced rapidly, indigenous languages remain largely absent from digital spaces, creating barriers to education, communication, and cultural preservation for their communities.

communities.name: Che Wong
communities.subtitle: Orang Asli Community, Malaysia
communities.description: The Che Wong are an indigenous group residing in the rainforests of Pahang, Malaysia. Their language carries unique knowledge about forest ecosystems and traditional practices passed down through generations.

communities.name: Temuan
communities.subtitle: Orang Asli Community, Malaysia
communities.description: The Temuan people are one of the largest Orang Asli subgroups in Peninsular Malaysia. Their language and oral traditions contain rich cultural heritage and traditional ecological knowledge.

communities.name: Iban
communities.subtitle: Indigenous Community, Sarawak
communities.description: The Iban are the largest indigenous group in Sarawak, Malaysian Borneo. While their language has more speakers than some other indigenous languages, documenting dialectal variations and traditional vocabulary remains crucial.

communities.subtitle: Bidayuh Subgroup, Sarawak
communities.description: The Bukar Sadong are a subgroup of the Bidayuh people in Sarawak. Their distinct language and cultural practices represent an important part of Borneo's indigenous heritage.

research.headerSubtitle: Cutting-edge work across linguistics, technology, and ethics to preserve indigenous languages
research.area1Intro: Building comprehensive records of indigenous languages through systematic data collection and community collaboration.

area1Cards.title: Audio Recordings
area1Cards.description: High-quality audio recordings capture pronunciation, intonation, and natural speech patterns. These recordings build a foundational understanding of each language's phonology and prosody.

area1Cards.title: IndigiSEA Recorder App
area1Cards.description: Our custom-built mobile application enables offline recording in remote areas without internet connectivity, allowing community members to contribute recordings from anywhere.

area1Cards.title: Vocabulary & Sentences
area1Cards.description: Systematic collection of day-to-day vocabulary, thematic sentences, and natural conversations. Words and sentences are generated through structured elicitation sessions with native speakers.

research.area2Intro: Building the technological foundation to support indigenous languages in the digital age, from data collection tools to language models.
research.area2Body: Our contributions address the fundamental challenge of data scarcity that has historically prevented indigenous languages from benefiting from advances in language technology. We develop novel approaches for low-resource language processing and create tools that can operate in environments with limited connectivity.

area2Stats.label: Resource Languages
area2Stats.description: Developing techniques specifically for languages with limited digital presence and training data.

area2Stats.label: Language Models
area2Stats.description: Creating efficient, compact models that can run on limited hardware and work offline.

area2Stats.label: Bottleneck Solutions
area2Stats.description: Innovative approaches to overcome the fundamental challenge of limited training data, including transfer learning from related languages and data augmentation techniques.

research.area3Intro: Ensuring that language preservation efforts respect community rights and cultural protocols while advancing digital inclusion.

area3Principles.title: Community Ownership
area3Principles.description: Data belongs to the communities from which it originates

area3Principles.title: Informed Consent
area3Principles.description: Clear, culturally appropriate consent processes for all participants

area3Principles.title: Cultural Sensitivity
area3Principles.description: Respecting sacred knowledge and cultural protocols in data handling

area3Principles.title: Benefit Sharing
area3Principles.description: Ensuring communities benefit from the research and tools developed

area3Principles.title: Data Governance
area3Principles.description: Community-led decisions on data access, use, and storage

home.heroTitle: Merapatkan Jurang Digital bagi Bahasa Orang Asal Asia Tenggara
home.heroSubtitle: Dengan lebih 800 bahasa di Malaysia dan Indonesia, kebanyakannya terancam kritikal, IndigiSEA akan membina rakyat, proses, dan perkongsian yang penting untuk kelestarian linguistik jangka panjang. Projek ini akan membangunkan rangka kerja beretika, model penyelidikan penyertaan, dan platform digital yang memupuk akses, inovasi, dan kepimpinan komuniti untuk memajukan masa depan digital beretika bagi bahasa Orang Asal.

about.headerSubtitle: Memahami cabaran dan pendekatan kami dalam memelihara bahasa Orang Asal Asia Tenggara
problemParagraphs: Asia Tenggara mempunyai kepelbagaian linguistik yang luar biasa, dengan lebih 800 bahasa dituturkan di Malaysia dan Indonesia sahaja. Namun begitu, warisan kaya ini menghadapi ancaman yang belum pernah berlaku.

Kebanyakan bahasa ini terancam kritikal, dengan bilangan penutur yang semakin berkurangan dan dokumentasi yang terhad. Apabila generasi tua meninggal dunia, pengetahuan linguistik, tradisi budaya, dan pandangan dunia yang tidak ternilai berisiko hilang selama-lamanya.

Jurang digital memburukkan lagi krisis ini. Walaupun teknologi maju dengan pesat, bahasa Orang Asal sebahagian besarnya tidak hadir dalam ruang digital, mewujudkan halangan kepada pendidikan, komunikasi, dan pemeliharaan budaya bagi komuniti mereka.

Kami membangunkan pendekatan baharu untuk pemprosesan bahasa sumber rendah dan mencipta alat yang boleh beroperasi dalam persekitaran dengan sambungan terhad.
